title: skill-compiler: compile skills into validated cached adapters, with pool-attested pass verification
body: Port of fork PR 12 (the contributor's fork) onto current upstream/main. Rebuilt in a worktree by cherry-picking only the branch's own commits, so it carries none of the fork main's history. Own test suites run locally and pass on the branch. Companion upstream PRs replace the fifteen fork PRs that were opened in the wrong place.
source: On 2026-10-22 the maintainer delegated judging and fixing findings to the review loop. These are agent judgments, not individually maintainer-confirmed labels. The original gpt-6-astra session checked every final finding and excluded proposals, carrying forward earlier decisions. It and the coordinator reproduced NUL input corruption; the coordinator additionally reproduced false VERIFIED from NUL in observed evidence. Case base is the PR merge-base; integration target is eab04ad4097fb2030f27bee6026e24f57289f12d. GitHub reported no body edit history; identifying names are generalized. Prior collection kept30 decisions and omitted192 under its cap, with3 fit answers. Three agent-mode rounds were completed. The maintainer subsequently authorized a human-mode review after repair, and resumed work on 2026-10-22 with a preference for simple maintainable fixes. Final fixes were verified on macOS Bash 3.2 and Linux Bash 5.2 against the branch and exact current-main integration. The published branch includes a normal merge of main before separate NUL and CI commits.

findings.label: valid
findings.what: PR title still promises adapters although this tool saves validation reports.

found_by.text: The change does not compile skills into adapters; title promises behavior the tool explicitly does not do. The PR title says "skill-compiler: compile skills into validated cached adapters, with pool-attested pass verification". What ships is a validator: README.md lines 9-11 state explicitly "It does not train an adapter, alter the skill, or add examples to `skills show`", and SKILL.md lines 180-181 say "This produces validation reports, not trained adapters or automatically loaded examples." No adapter is produced anywhere in the 1581-line script; `compile` writes `<skill>.md`, `<skill>.json`, `<skill>.json.prov` and `pool-<skill>.json` only. The description gives no hint that the diff is a large new validator rather than the adapter compiler its title names.

README title and opening paragraph describe a "skill validator" rather than the skill-compiler the PR adds. The file is the reference for the new `skill-compiler` tool, but its H1 is "# Skill validator reference" and the paragraph calls it "It calls `llm` to propose cases, runs each through `shellm`, and saves results. It does not train an adapter...". That contradicts the PR title and SKILL.md, which advertise compiling skills into validated cached adapters; a reader looking for the compile step the PR adds finds a document that says no adapter is produced and never names the `compile` command semantics in the title. Rename the heading to the tool's name and word the opening so it matches what `compile` actually does.

findings.label: valid
findings.what: Direct harness invocation requires a fresh output root but diagnoses reuse poorly.

found_by.text: STUBS.mkdir() without exist_ok fails on a reused ROOT. The module does `ROOT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` but then `STUBS.mkdir()` without `exist_ok=True`. Any second run pointing at the same root directory (a rerun after a crash, a retry in the harness, or the same ROOT passed twice) raises FileExistsError at import and the whole regression suite aborts before printing anything.

Case root mkdir is not idempotent, unlike the mktemp-based sibling test script. teacher_failures (line 523) and bracketed_prose (later in the file) both do `Case('teacher-invalid-json')`/`Case(...)` as a second Case inside one check function, after earlier Cases in the same function have already created fixtures. Because Case.__init__ calls self.root.mkdir() without exist_ok (line 123), this only works because the names differ; the pattern makes re-runs of the module against an existing ROOT aborts, unlike the sibling driver tests/test_skill_compiler.sh, which uses a fresh mktemp -d per run (line 24). If a full pass leaves ROOT/teacher-invalid-json behind, a re-run raises FileExistsError and the check is reported as failed rather than exercising the compiler.

direct_cache calls copy.mkdir() and Case('direct-cache') without checking ROOT reuse, so a re-run aborts before restoring SC. ROOT is created with exist_ok=True at line 15, but direct_cache uses copy.mkdir() (line 530) and Case() always calls self.root.mkdir() (line 123) without exist_ok. When the same scratch ROOT is reused (REGRESSION_FILTER re-run, or a rerun of the suite in the same directory) these raise FileExistsError. The finally at line 536 does restore SC in that case, but the case can never be exercised on a reused root while all other cases survive it. Use exist_ok=True or write into a unique per-run directory.

findings.what: Echo-filter negative assertion is `any(...) | not`, so it passes whenever any single non-echo entry exists. Line 428's second jq filter is `[.entries[].line] | any(...) | not`. `any(cond)` over an array is true when at least one element matches, so `. | not` only proves that NOT ALL entries are echoes; it does not prove that no echo line survives. If a filter regression re-admitted `Notes: A1 B2 ...` alongside the near-miss line, `any` would be true and the check would still pass unless the echo lines were literally the only entries. The first half (`any(. == "Verdict: ...")`) is correct; the second needs `all(. != "Notes: ..." and . != "Intervals: ...")`.

findings.label: valid
findings.what: History vocabulary sent to the teacher could be called out explicitly as provider input.

found_by.text: Auto-harvest greps and parses the live trajectory store, pulling other identities' output into the teacher prompt. `grep -rlF --include='*.jsonl' -m1 "$script" "$traj_dir"` scans `${SKILL_HARVEST_TRAJ_DIR:-${TRAJ_DIR:-<state-home>/trajectories}}` — the live trajectory store by default (SKILL_AUTO_HARVEST is on unless set to 0, line 949) — and the harvest Python then keeps every stdout line of matching runs in `entries`. Those lines are handed to `llm` as the phrase pool and written to the shared cache `<state-home>/skill-compiler/history/pool-history-<skill>.json`, so text produced by other identities/sessions (which may contain user data) is sent to a third-party model provider and persisted on disk whenever `compile`/`pool` runs. The README documents this, but nothing warns that the default reads the live store.
